documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: VIN with a matching decode, an all-in dealer price, and a history summary (single owner, no reported accident). The maintenance half is absent. There are no receipts for the 'full service', rear brakes or lift install, and no evidence on SAI, KDSS or rust.

condition.rationale: Nothing is stated wrong. The photo supports new wheels, tires and a lift, but nothing establishes the drivetrain, cooling, SAI or underbody condition. 'Amazing shape' is prose.

price_value.rationale: The $31,495 asking price is roughly 35% above the $19,501 fair-value midpoint and above the top of its range. A 2014 Luxury at the same mileage sold for $28,500 in June. The build accessories do not command that premium.

mission_fit.rationale: It supplies real capability the RX lacks: body-on-frame 4WD, a roof rack suited to a rooftop tent, and an awning. However, the ask sits above the $27,000 max price, and the lift and all-terrain tires trade on-road refinement for off-road hardware the buyer does not plan to use.

logistics.rationale: The car is in California, about 372 miles away, at a dealer, with CA smog and registration straightforward. PPI access is not stated but should be arrangeable locally.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: It is a refresh-year car with a tasteful, coherent mild overland build. That is offset by the Base trim, the ordinary colour, and a dealer build rather than documented originality.

positives: VIN published and the decode matches: a 2014 GX 460 with the 1UR-FE V8 and full-time 4WD.
The history summary shows a single owner and no reported accident or damage (subject to seeing the full report).
The roof rack and awning directly support the rooftop-tent camping intent.
Claimed new ICON suspension, wheels, KO3 tires and rear brakes; the lift, wheels and fresh-looking tires are visible in the photo.
California dealer with an all-in price including dealer fees, so a CA smog certificate is the dealer's obligation.
concerns: Observed: the asking price of $31,495 sits well above the mileage-adjusted fair value of $16,758–$23,430, and the premium rests on bolt-on accessories.
Observed: a 2-2.5in lift with new UCAs, installed by a flip builder with no alignment sheet or install invoice; this raises CV, ball-joint and KDSS-integration questions.
Unverified: secondary air injection pump and valve history (ask for any P2440/P2442 history or a replacement invoice; scan for pending codes).
Unverified: KDSS equipment and status (confirm whether fitted; inspect accumulators and cylinders for leaks, lean and lift-bracket fitment).
Unverified: valley-plate coolant and timing-cover seepage at 126k (inspect at the PPI).
Unverified: 'fully serviced' with no receipts; transmission, transfer case, differential and coolant service history unknown (ask for invoices).

SAI system condition and code history

seller_questions: Can you send the full Carfax/AutoCheck, including service entries and the state where the car was registered?
What exactly did 'fully serviced' include? Please send the invoice with parts, fluids and mileage.
Does this car have KDSS? If so, what brackets or adjustments were used with the ICON Stage 2 kit, and has the system been bled and leveled?
Has the secondary air injection pump or valve ever been replaced, or thrown P2440/P2442? Can you send a current scan-tool report showing no stored or pending codes?
Can you provide the ICON install invoice and the post-install four-wheel alignment printout?
What are the DOT date codes on the five tires, and is the spare matched?
Can you send photos of the frame rails, rear crossmember and valley area behind the engine, plus a cold-start video?
Were the original suspension components retained, and are they included?
Will you allow an independent pre-purchase inspection at a Toyota/Lexus specialist in San Diego before any deposit?
When were the transmission fluid, transfer case, differentials and coolant last changed?
ppi_focus: Scan all modules for SAI codes (P2440/P2442/P0418), including pending and readiness monitors; listen to the SAI pump on cold start.
Establish whether KDSS is fitted; check accumulators, cylinders and lines for leaks, and check lean and bracket fitment after the lift.
Look for valley-plate coolant residue at the rear of the block and timing-cover seepage.
Check CV axle angles and boots, ball joints and tie rods under the 2.5in front lift, and verify the ICON UCA install and torque.
Inspect the frame, crossmembers and hitch area for rust, towing wear and off-road damage.
Examine the roof rack mounting points and roof for leaks or stress, given the intended rooftop tent use.
Check transmission, transfer case and differential fluid condition, and test the 4WD low-range and center-diff lock.
Read tire date codes and check alignment and wear pattern.
what_would_change_verdict: A negotiated price near the fair-value range, around $23k–25k all-in, would materially improve value.
Invoices showing the SAI, KDSS and fluid services, plus a clean specialist PPI, would lift documentation and condition.
A professional install invoice and alignment sheet for the lift would reduce modification risk.
Evidence of SAI codes, KDSS leaks, valley-plate coolant or frame rust would push it down.
evidence.mission_note: A GX460 with a rack and awning genuinely adds rooftop-tent and 4WD capability the RX 350 lacks, so it fits the capability branch in principle. The lift and all-terrain build overshoot the stated needs, and the ask is above the max price, so fit depends on price and proof of condition.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2014 GX 460 Base, and the history summary shows one owner and no reported accident. The dealer describes a fresh ICON Stage 2 lift, a Gobi rack, an ARB awning, new wheels and KO3 tires, and one attached photo shows a silver refresh-year GX with that build. Most other attached photos show different dealer inventory. Maintenance is limited to 'fully serviced' and 'rear brake job', with no receipts. The model's key weak points (secondary air injection, KDSS integration with the lift, valley-plate coolant, frame condition) are all unaddressed. The $31,495 ask includes dealer fees but sits roughly $8k above the top of the mileage-adjusted fair-value range, and a comparable 2014 Luxury at 126.5k sold for $28,500. No faults are disclosed, so no known-work estimate is established. The value gap rests on accessories rather than documented mechanical renewal.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer for the full history report, the service and lift-install invoices, the alignment printout, a current scan report and underbody photos, and confirm that an independent Toyota/Lexus PPI in San Diego is allowed before any deposit.
